summary: Boxtel is a small Noord-Brabant town where street parking in the centre is paid (0.21 euros per 12 minutes, about 1.05 euros an hour, in the first two hours and 0.41 euros per 12 minutes after that, unchanged since 2024 under the 2026 ordinance), with a two-hour parking-disc (blue) zone around the station and in Breukelen-Zuid and resident and business permits at 129 to 478 euros a year. The council's 2025 mobility programme and environment vision want a car-light centre with long-stay parking at the edges and the station developed into a regional mobility hub, and a new parking-norms note of January 2026 introduces lower car norms near the station and a 10,000 euro per space contribution fund for the centre. The park-and-ride at Van Salmstraat (193 spaces, open 24/7) appears on Q-Park's website as a Q-Park facility, although the national open-data register still carries an older record naming NS. A survey from October 2016 found no overall shortage in the centre but a distribution problem at busy moments, and no newer published utilisation figures were found. In September 2026 the municipality designated 48 charging-only bays in Boxtel and Liempde under a province-wide Vattenfall contract.

items.text: The Boxtel council adopted the Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026 on 4 November 2025, with levy from 1 January 2026. Paid street parking costs 0.21 euros per 12 minutes in the first and second hour (about 1.05 euros an hour) and 0.41 euros per 12 minutes after that, unchanged from the 2024 and 2025 rates.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Boxtel)

items.text: Permit tariffs in the 2026 table are 32.25 euros per quarter (129 euros a year) for a plate-bound permit for part of the paid area, 70.25 euros per quarter (281 euros a year) for the whole area, and 119.50 euros per quarter (478 euros a year) for a non-plate-bound permit for the whole area. The 2025 ordinance had 31.25, 68.25 and 116.25 euros per quarter for the same types.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Boxtel)

items.text: Earlier versions of the Boxtel parking-tax ordinance show the hourly rate was 0.20 euros per 14 minutes (about 0.86 euros an hour) until the end of 2022, 0.20 euros per 12 minutes (1.00 euros an hour) in 2023, and 0.21 euros per 12 minutes from 2024. The long-stay rate after two hours moved from 0.40 to 0.41 euros per 12 minutes in 2024.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2015, versions 2015-2024 (Boxtel)

items.text: On 23 January 2026 Boxtel published a new Parkeernormennota for cars and bikes in the Gemeenteblad, replacing the 2007 norms. It adds bicycle-parking norms, rules for car-sharing, and a new sub-area Centrum Stationsgebied near the station with minimum (lower) car norms, described as steering rather than following parking demand. The municipality plans a parking-pressure measurement in the centre once every three years.
items.source_title: Parkeernormennota voor auto en fiets Gemeente Boxtel (Gemeenteblad 2026, 29605)

items.text: Under the 2026 norms note, developers in the centre who cannot provide the required parking on their own land can pay 10,000 euros per missing space into a municipal fund 'Bereikbaarheid centrumgebied Boxtel', used for shared car and bike parking or public transport. This needs spare public capacity nearby (usable up to 85 percent) shown by a parking survey, and the note cites the 'Visie op de Bezoekerseconomie 2022-2030' that rates the fragmented centre parking as a weakness.
items.source_title: Parkeernormennota voor auto en fiets Gemeente Boxtel (Gemeenteblad 2026, 29605)

items.text: The Omgevingsvisie Boxtel, adopted by the council on 4 February 2025 and published on 12 March 2025, says Boxtel station is to be developed into a mobility hub with more space for shared mobility. It states that car access and parking remain important but have lower priority and are moved more towards the edges, and it announces area programmes for the town and the station area (front and back of the station).

The Programma Duurzame Mobiliteit Boxtel 'Op weg naar 2040' (January 2025) aims for a car-light centre where cars drive around the centre and long-stay parking is at its edges, and says the municipality does not size parking for peak days or events. It states that a blue zone around the existing station keeps out long-stay train travellers, and that new parking policy will look at tariff differentiation, car-sharing parking, smart parking systems and regular parking-pressure measurements.
items.source_title: Programma Duurzame Mobiliteit Boxtel, Op weg naar 2040 (January 2025)

items.text: The programme says the province names Boxtel station as a regional node and the municipality wants to make it a regional mobility hub with province and region. It treats use of the existing station car parking as part of the trip to the train, and mentions the P+R on the west side of the station in connection with links from the villages.
items.source_title: Programma Duurzame Mobiliteit Boxtel, Op weg naar 2040 (January 2025)

items.text: By a decision dated 21 September 2026 (Gemeenteblad of 25 September 2026), Boxtel designated 48 parking spaces for charging only, at various locations in Boxtel and Liempde; the draft of 29 June 2026 had 54, and 9 locations were dropped after objections. Sites follow a province-wide contract with Vattenfall, and a second bay is reserved at a post once it uses at least 3,500 kWh.
items.source_title: Verkeersbesluit Aanwijzen parkeerplaatsen opladen elektrische voertuigen diverse locaties Boxtel en Liempde (Gemeenteblad 2026, 450690)

items.text: Boxtel's policy rules for public charge points, published on 4 September 2019, take a facilitating role: charging bays are reserved by traffic decision, and payment is still due when charging in paid-parking areas (a parking disc in disc zones). The rules also cite a Nuon/Heijmans contract running until end 2019, so they are dated.
items.source_title: Beleidsregels Openbare Oplaadpalen voor elektrische voertuigen (Gemeenteblad 2019, 217047)

items.text: A parking-pressure and parking-motive survey in the first week of October 2016 (Trajan, report of 28 November 2016) found no overall shortage in the centre and Breukelen Zuid, because public spaces were never all occupied at once, but a distribution problem with some locations above the accepted pressure at busy times (targets 85 percent in mixed areas, 90 percent in residential areas). This is old data, quoted in the 2017 parking vision.

Since 24 August 2017 (still listed as in force in October 2026) the decision on parking-disc exemptions in the Centrum/Breukelen Zuid zone has been mandated to the director of P1 On Street B.V., under a service agreement of 28 July 2017 after a tender.

According to the 2017 vision, Boxtel agreed with NS in 2013 to introduce permit parking around the NS car park on the centre side of the station in return for NS bicycle storage. In December 2016 they agreed to regulate the Parallelweg Noord car park (64 spaces) so that P+R travellers use the NS facility on the west side of the station.

A traffic decision of 6 June 2017 set a two-hour parking-disc zone in Breukelen-Zuid and the centre west of the Dommel (including Stationsplein, Stationsstraat, Prins Hendrikstraat and Parallelweg Noord), valid Monday to Thursday 9.00-18.00, Friday 9.00-21.00 and Saturday 9.00-17.30. It also withdrew paid parking in several streets near the station. Later changes to the zone were not checked.
items.source_title: Verkeersbesluit Instellen parkeerschijfzone Breukelen-Zuid en Centrum (westzijde Dommel), 6 June 2017

items.text: By a traffic decision dated 20 March 2025 (published 25 March 2025), Boxtel made the Stationsstraat between Molenstraat and Prins Bernhardstraat a pedestrian zone: cyclists allowed, mopeds not, loading 7.00-13.00. Residents and businesses with private parking reachable only through the zone can obtain exemptions.

Q-Park's Boxtel page, read on 21 October 2026, lists one facility, P+R Van Salmstraat (5281 RS Boxtel), with 193 spaces, open 24/7 for arrival and departure, and a reduced rate for same-day domestic train travellers. The tariff widget did not load, so no current price was read.
items.source_title: Q-Park P+R Van Salmstraat (page read 21 October 2026)

items.text: The national parking register (NPR) open data, read on 21 October 2026, holds two records for the Van Salmstraat P+R: one naming Nederlandse Spoorwegen as operator with 193 spaces and a tariff of 0.77 euros per hour and 5.41 euros per day from May 2021 (record last updated 12 December 2024), and an older limited-access record naming Q-Park. The tariff data are therefore old and the operator entry is inconsistent with Q-Park's own page.
items.source_title: NPR open data, P+R Van Salmstraat (Boxtel) static record

items.text: On 10 December 2024 the PvdA-GroenLinks group tabled an amendment to the area vision for the station surroundings, calling for an integrated vision for both sides of the station soon and noting that the Salmstraat P+R site could become a live-work tower with an underground car park. This was a council amendment proposal; the outcome of the vote and any follow-up were not found.

gaps: https://www.boxtel.nl/in-de-gemeente/parkeren, https://www.boxtel.nl/aanvragen-regelen-en-melden/vergunningen/parkeervergunning and other boxtel.nl pages returned a 503 maintenance error on 21 October 2026, so the current municipal pages on blue-zone hours, paid-parking areas (Bijlage a map of the ordinance is an image) and permits were not read; the zone hours given are from a 2017 traffic decision.
Current Q-Park tariffs for P+R Van Salmstraat: the Q-Park page's tariff widget did not load; third-party listing portals were not used.

No recent (post-2016) parking-pressure or utilisation report for the centre was found; the 2026 norms note says a measurement is made every three years but the results were not located. Council-information portal boxtel.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl search and report lists are JavaScript-rendered and could not be read, so council papers on parking since 2024 (raadsvoorstel of 30 September 2025 on the tariffs, Visie op de Bezoekerseconomie 2022-2030, Parkeervisie follow-ups) were not opened.

No source found on new, closed or refurbished centre car parks, on a concrete P+R or station-area parking project, or on the outcome of the December 2024 amendment (Salmstraat P+R as tower with underground car park). The Markt reconstruction and the compensating parking facility planned in 2017 were not confirmed.

No local press (Brabants Dagblad, Omroep Brabant, local weeklies) was read: the Omroep Brabant article on the 54 charging bays labels itself automatically compiled and was not used; the web-search budget ran out before local news could be searched.

The Omgevingsvisie, Gemeenteblad PDFs and the 2026 EV decision were read in full for the cited passages only; annexes with charging locations (bijlage 1 and 2 of the EV decision) were not available as text, so whether any bays are at the station or centre car parks is unknown.
